Use **`append_server_name`** in `xcsh_workload`:

```text
stateful_service.advertise_options.advertise_on_public.multi_ports.ports.http_loadbalancer.https_auto_cert.append_server_name
```

It preserves an existing `Server` header and sets your configured value only when absent. Do **not** use `server_name`, which overwrites existing values.

The optional string conflicts with `server_name`, `default_header`, and `pass_through`.

Verified in bundled provider **v12.4.0**: [exact field reference](xcsh://terraform-documentation/documentation/resources/workload/properties/stateful_service/advertise_options/advertise_on_public/multi_ports/ports/http_loadbalancer/https_auto_cert/index.md?view=context#schema-stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_on_public--multi_ports--ports--http_loadbalancer--https_auto_cert--append_server_name).

Use **`server_name`** in `xcsh_workload` at:

```text
stateful_service.advertise_options.advertise_on_public.multi_ports.ports.http_loadbalancer.https_auto_cert.server_name
```

It sets the `Server` response-header value and **overwrites any existing value**. Unlike `append_server_name`, it does not preserve the existing header.

It is an optional string, with a provider-enforced maximum length of 8,096, and conflicts with `append_server_name`, `default_header`, and `pass_through`.

Verified in bundled provider **v12.4.0**: [exact field reference](xcsh://terraform-documentation/documentation/resources/workload/properties/stateful_service/advertise_options/advertise_on_public/multi_ports/ports/http_loadbalancer/https_auto_cert/index.md?view=context#schema-stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_on_public--multi_ports--ports--http_loadbalancer--https_auto_cert--server_name).
